title: How do chicks know who their mother is?
examples: Why do ducklings follow their mother?
Can a duckling imprint on a person?

explain.say: Ducklings and goslings hatch able to walk, and within hours they follow their mother everywhere. They learn who she is by imprinting: locking on to the first moving, calling thing they meet.

draw.text: How do chicks know who their mother is?

explain.say: In the 1930s Konrad Lorenz showed that goslings hatched away from their mother would imprint on him instead, following him in a line as if he were their parent.

explain.say: Imprinting works best during a short sensitive period. In mallard ducklings it was strongest around 13 to 16 hours after hatching and much weaker after about two days, as chicks become wary of new things.
Imprinting keeps chicks close to the adult who will protect them. It can also shape later life: birds raised by people may court people when grown, so keepers rearing rare cranes wear crane costumes.

faq.q: Can a duckling imprint on a person?
faq.a: Yes. If the first moving, calling thing a duckling or gosling meets is a person, it will follow that person as if they were its mother. Konrad Lorenz famously had goslings following him everywhere.
asks: Will a chick follow a human?
What did Konrad Lorenz do with geese?

faq.a: Imprinting is a fast kind of learning in young animals, especially birds that can walk soon after hatching. During a short window they learn to recognise and follow a parent, and the bond lasts.
asks: Why do ducklings follow their mother?
How do baby birds know their parents?

faq.q: Why is there a time limit on imprinting?
faq.a: Imprinting happens during a sensitive period soon after hatching. As chicks get older they become fearful of new things and run from them instead, so the window for imprinting closes.
Douglas Spalding described it in chicks in the 1870s, and Konrad Lorenz studied it in geese in the 1930s. Lorenz shared the 1973 Nobel Prize for his work on animal behaviour.

faq.q: Why do people raising cranes wear costumes?
faq.a: Birds that imprint on humans may later try to court people instead of their own kind. Keepers raising rare whooping cranes wear crane costumes and use crane-head puppets so the chicks imprint on cranes.
asks: Why do zookeepers dress as birds?

facts: Konrad Lorenz shared the 1973 Nobel Prize with Karl von Frisch and Nikolaas Tinbergen for discoveries about animal behaviour.
